title: 1975 Shrine concert: Joe Williams stranded in London, and copyist Bill Hughes
summary: Jones raced the copyists to conduct for Randy Crawford while Joe Williams was fogged in, praising the Hughes copyists.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: You know, just for acts. And then another one was Randy Crawford. I can't even think of the -- this was on Warner Brothers. I can't think of what the name of the song was, or whatever the songs were. Oh, I remember. This is a thing at the auditorium -- well, it's further back than what you're asking. I think Quincy Jones, George Benson --
Oh, the World Jazz Association concert at the Shrine Auditorium, in 1975?
Was it that far back?
Uh-huh. November, 1975.
I remember it was in November.
That's right. You conducted --
Yeah.
-- for Randy and what else? Didn't you do something else too on that show?
No, I don't think so. And I conducted once
for Joe Williams, but that was a different show, right at the same place.
Joe was supposed to be on that concert, but he got --
Stranded in London.
Stranded in London, yeah.

When I got there, the -- my schedule was running very tight at the copyist's office, and I began to start pacing the floor, and of course I've got the best in town, the best I've ever had, and they got it done, and when I got to the stage door, there was John Levy outside, pacing the sidewalk. Said, "Joe's in London and Randy's music's not here, our conductor's not here." He started scratching his head, you know?
(Laughter)
But I got there. He wasn't too upset. He had to be a little tense. And he said, "Well, don't you worry about your problems. We've got another big one, because Joe Williams is not going to be here."
Yeah, it was what, snowing in London or something.
I think it was fogged in.
Oh. Something. Yeah, I remember we got the call.
Yeah.
Late. And your copyist that you regard so highly is Bill Hughes, right?
Yeah, that's right. He's -- all that staff over there, they're like co-workers, you know?
Uh-huh.
More than just copyists. They're really orchestrators and everything. And how they get that work out, I do not know. They have all the major shows, you know.
Uh-huh. Yeah, I know, it's amazing, the volume that comes out of there and the high quality, apparently, all the time.
That's right. That's the reason they're in business. The greatest reference, you know?
